reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any complete real inner-product space (a real Hilbert space), with no finite-dimensionality assumption, and let f:E→ℝ be twice continuously Fréchet differentiable on all of E. For every x,v∈E, the inner product of ∇f(x+v)−∇f(x) with v equals the Lebesgue integral from 0 to 1 of the second Fréchet derivative at x+t v evaluated on (v,v): ⟨∇f(x+v)−∇f(x),v⟩ = ∫₀¹ D²f(x+t v)[v,v] dt. The gradient is the Riesz representative of the first Fréchet derivative. The integral is the oriented real interval integral, here with endpoints 0 and 1. There are no restrictions on x or v and no convexity or sign assumptions.
objects: E, f, x, v, the gradient of f, and the second Fréchet derivative of f.
domains: E is a complete real inner-product space; f:E→ℝ; x,v∈E; t∈ℝ is integrated from 0 to 1 against Lebesgue measure.
quantifiers: Universal over E and f satisfying the assumptions, then universal over x and v.
assumptions: f is C² on all E. Completeness and real inner-product structure are global assumptions.
conclusion: ⟨∇f(x+v)−∇f(x),v⟩ = ∫₀¹ D²f(x+t v)[v,v] dt for all x,v.
scopes: Regularity and the asserted property hold on the entire displayed space, not merely on a subset or at selected points.
